digest.top_line: Nine-trial NACT pool (N=10,075): 5-yr LRR 4.1% with pCR vs 9.5% without (HR 3.33), TNBC non-pCR 18.5%, the risk group to target for post-NACT RT.
digest.tldr: All-breast, all-retrospective day on locoregional risk for RT selection. After NACT, residual disease and TNBC drive LRR (non-pCR HR 3.33; CPS+EG 5-yr LRR-free 71% to 99%), and RNI's adjusted LRR HR 0.497 rests on a null univariate split. With upfront mastectomy and no RT, RS ≥18 (10-yr LRR 16.5% vs 9.7%) and age <45 with >25% nodes positive flag LRR risk.

sites.intro: Five retrospective or pooled cohorts on who needs PMRT or RNI. None randomised RT, so every RT signal here is confounded by indication.

studies.name: 21-gene Recurrence Score and locoregional recurrence in node-positive breast cancer (SWOG 8814 correlative)
studies.tldr: 10-yr LRR 16.5% vs 9.7% for RS ≥18 vs <18 (P=.02) in ER/PR+ node-positive breast; widest split at 1-3 nodes after mastectomy without RT.
details: 🔍 Retrospective translational cohort from phase 3 SWOG S8814 (tamoxifen alone vs CAF-T), N=316 postmenopausal ER/PR+ node-positive women
🔍 Excluded mastectomy + RT (n=37), BCS without RT (n=9), unknown surgery (n=5)
📊 Prespecified primary analysis (continuous RS, multivariable) null: HR 1.14 per 10-point increase (95% CI 0.97-1.35, P=.11)

details.text: 📊 10-yr actuarial LRR by RS category (secondary analysis, cut at 18)
📐 LRR multivariable model

details: 📊 Nodal burden: 10-yr LRR 9.0% with 1-3 nodes vs 24.4% with ≥4 (P=.002)
⚠️ ≥4 nodes after mastectomy: low RS did not lower LRR (25.9% vs 27.0%), so no PMRT omission signal in pN2a

details.text: 🔗 vs NSABP B-28 (all pts got chemo, no PMRT allowed), 10-yr LRR
subdetails: S8814 1-3 node mastectomy pts with RS ≥18 ran higher at 11.1%

details: ⚠️ Cut point of 18 confirmed as optimal only post hoc; subsets exploratory, not adjusted for multiplicity
⚠️ BCS arm uninformative: 6 LRR events total (2/29 low vs 4/35 intermediate/high RS)
🔍 Mean LRR follow-up 8.2 y; median 8.7 y (IQR 7.0-10.2) for pts without LRR

verdict.rationale: Retrospective correlative of a chemo trial with nonrandomized RT. Prespecified continuous-RS analysis null (P=.11); the cut at 18 was confirmed post hoc; nodal subsets exploratory with few events.
verdict.audience: Postmenopausal ER/PR+ node-positive breast, mastectomy without PMRT

studies.significance: In mastectomy-only pts with 1-3 nodes, 10-yr LRR was 1.5% at RS <18 vs 11.1% at RS ≥18 (P=.051, n=165). That gives the PMRT de-escalation hypothesis TailorRT is testing a biological basis. At ≥4 nodes low RS offered no protection (25.9% vs 27.0%), so a low score is no reason to drop PMRT in pN2a.
studies.monday_clinic: In a postmenopausal ER/PR+ pN1 pt after mastectomy with RS ≥18, this argues against treating the score as reassurance when discussing PMRT; it does not support omitting PMRT at RS <18 outside a trial, and does not apply to ≥4 positive nodes.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Retrospective translational cohort** within phase 3 SWOG S8814, which enrolled 1989-1995. RT use was **not randomized**: it was expected after BCS and left to physician discretion after mastectomy. Reported under REMARK guidelines.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Postmenopausal, ER/PR+, node-positive** women from the tamoxifen-only and CAF-T arms who had RS assayed. Final **N=316**: BCS + RT or mastectomy without RT. Pts who received PMRT were excluded, so the mastectomy cohort is the group whose physicians judged RT unnecessary.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Tamoxifen 20 mg daily for 5 y, alone or after 6 cycles of CAF (CAF-T). The concurrent CAF + tamoxifen arm was excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** LRR (breast, chest wall, axillary, infraclavicular, supraclavicular or IMN), censored at distant recurrence or death. The primary analysis used continuous RS; the secondary analysis compared RS <18 vs ≥18.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: The **continuous-RS primary analysis was not significant** (P=.11). The categorical split and the subset tables carry the signal.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: **Direction agrees with NSABP B-28**, where RS also independently predicted LRR. Absolute LRR at 1-3 nodes was higher here than in B-28, which treated every pt with chemo and allowed no PMRT. MA.20 and EORTC 22922 show a nodal RT DFS benefit even where LRR is low, so LRR alone may underestimate what RT buys.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents postmenopausal ER/PR+ pN1 pts after mastectomy without PMRT, on tamoxifen-based therapy. Does not represent pN2a disease, BCS pts, or pts on modern systemic therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: **Treatment era:** CAF and tamoxifen only, with no taxanes or AIs, both of which may lower baseline LRR. LRR was censored at distant recurrence, which can undercount local failures. The ≥4-node mastectomy subset had no n reported.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: RS looks prognostic for LRR beyond nodal count, but **it cannot yet select pN1 pts for PMRT omission**. That question belongs to TailorRT (MA.39), which randomizes only low-RS pN1 pts. Nodal burden still dominates the risk at ≥4 nodes.

studies.interpretation:
The appeal of this analysis is that it asks a local-therapy question of a genomic assay built and validated for systemic decisions. The answer is suggestive, not conclusive. Its direction matches NSABP B-28, the other node-positive dataset where RS tracked locoregional failure, and the two cohorts complement each other. B-28 gave everyone chemotherapy and prohibited PMRT, so its mastectomy pts were unselected for local risk. In S8814, physicians could give PMRT to higher-risk pts, and those pts were removed. The mastectomy-alone group here is therefore one that clinicians had already judged low enough risk to skip RT. Even in that group, RS ≥18 identified a 1-3 node subset with 10-yr LRR of 11.1%. That is the most clinically relevant finding: a group many radiation oncologists would consider borderline carried a failure rate that most would treat.

The methodological picture should temper confidence in specific ways. The prespecified primary analysis, RS as a continuous term, did not reach significance. The positive results come from a dichotomy at 18 that the authors chose because of event counts and then confirmed post hoc as the best cut. Optimizing a cut point on the same data inflates the apparent separation. The headline 1-3 node contrast rests on 165 pts with a P value at the threshold, and the low-RS 1.5% figure reflects very few events. A rate that low invites over-reading: it is the estimate most likely to rise on replication. Censoring LRR at distant recurrence also means local failures that came after or alongside distant disease are not counted, which matters in a tamoxifen-era cohort with substantial distant failure.

The era cuts both ways. These pts received CAF or tamoxifen alone, with no taxanes, AIs, or modern nodal staging. Modern systemic therapy likely lowers the absolute LRR in every RS stratum. That could make low-RS omission safer than this cohort suggests, but it could also shrink the gap that makes RS discriminating. Whether RS adds information on top of contemporary pathology and therapy is not something a 1989-1995 cohort can settle.

The ≥4-node result is more robust in practical terms. LRR was about a quarter regardless of RS, so a favorable score does not offset nodal burden. That is consistent with PMRT staying standard for pN2a and aligns with the B-28 high-RS ≥4-node rate.

The last caution comes from the regional RT trials the authors cite. MA.20 and EORTC 22922 showed DFS gains from nodal irradiation despite modest LRR differences, so a low LRR estimate does not by itself show that RT adds nothing. Prognosis for LRR and benefit from RT are different questions. This study speaks only to the first. TailorRT, which randomizes low-RS pN1 pts, is the right test of the second, and this analysis is best read as the rationale for that trial rather than as a reason to act now.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: In mastectomy-only pN1 pts, 10-yr LRR was 1.5% at RS <18 vs 11.1% at RS ≥18 (P=.051), which supports the TailorRT hypothesis and argues for PMRT discussion at higher RS. At ≥4 nodes LRR was 25.9% vs 27.0% irrespective of RS, so pN2a PMRT is unchanged.

open_questions: Is PMRT omission safe in pN1 with low RS?
Does RS predict LRR under modern systemic therapy?
Does low LRR risk predict lack of RT DFS benefit?

studies.name: Locoregional recurrence after neoadjuvant chemotherapy: pooled analysis of nine trials
studies.tldr: 5-yr LRR 4.1% with pCR vs 9.5% without (multivariate HR 3.33); TNBC non-pCR 18.5%. Surgery type not independent after NACT.

details.text: 🔍 Exploratory IPD pooled analysis of 9 prospective GBG/AGO-B neoadjuvant trials (1998-2013), N=10,075

details: 🔍 Anthracycline/taxane NACT throughout; median f/u 67 mo
🔍 LRR as first event; distant recurrence, second malignancy and death treated as competing events (Gray / Fine-Gray)
📊 Overall 5-yr LRR: 7.8% after BCS vs 11.3% after mastectomy
📊 5-yr LRR by subtype: HR+/HER2- 6.0%, HR+/HER2+ 7.6%, HR-/HER2+ 10.5%, TNBC 14.4%

details.text: 📐 Multivariate: non-pCR HR 3.33 (95% CI 2.60-4.28); TNBC vs HR+/HER2- HR 2.72 (2.23-3.31); both p<0.001
📊 5-yr cumulative LRR, pCR vs non-pCR
📐 Independent LRR predictors within non-pCR pts
📊 After pCR, only cN+ trended toward higher LRR: HR 1.61 (0.99-2.61), p=0.054
📊 Mastectomy subgroup: non-pCR HR 4.00 (2.22-7.21); TNBC HR 2.48; cN+ HR 1.86

details: ⚠️ No patient-level RT data: PMRT and RNI use unknown, so RT's contribution to these rates cannot be separated
⚠️ Mastectomy LRR excess likely selection bias (higher-risk pts sent to mastectomy), per authors
⚠️ Pre-modern post-neoadjuvant therapy: older trials gave no anti-HER2 therapy to HER2+ pts; no T-DM1 or capecitabine escalation
🔗 vs EBCTCG NACT vs adjuvant meta-analysis: higher local recurrence with NACT, especially with suboptimal local therapy

verdict.rationale: Large mature IPD pool of prospective trials confirming known LRR predictors after NACT. Exploratory, prognostic only, and blind to RT delivery, so it cannot test an RT decision.
verdict.audience: Primary breast cancer after anthracycline/taxane NACT, incl. cT4a-d

studies.significance: Residual disease interacts with subtype: TNBC non-pCR LRR was 18.5% at 5y versus 4.2% after pCR, and HR-/HER2+ 14.8% vs 3.1%. With RT use unrecorded, these rates show where post-neoadjuvant RNI/PMRT escalation trials should focus. Within pCR, only cN+ trended toward risk (HR 1.61, p=0.054), relevant to node-based de-escalation.
studies.monday_clinic: In TNBC or HR-/HER2+ breast cancer with residual disease after NACT, this backs a high-LRR-risk read when weighing PMRT and nodal coverage; after pCR it shows low LRR across subtypes but cannot say whether omitting RT is safe, because RT delivery was not recorded.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Exploratory **individual-patient-data pooled analysis** of 9 prospective GBG/AGO-B neoadjuvant trials (GeparDuo through GeparSepto, PREPARE, TECHNO), 1998-2013. **N=10,075**; median follow-up **67 mo**. Pathologic response was analysed with landmarking (multivariate set N=9552).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Histologically confirmed primary invasive breast cancer, tumour mostly ≥2 cm; **locally advanced cT4a-c and inflammatory cT4d** eligible in all trials except GeparDuo. 63.6% HR-positive, 28.1% HER2-positive; pCR (ypT0 ypN0) in 20.4%.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Anthracycline/taxane-based NACT in all trials. Anti-HER2 therapy varied by trial (trastuzumab, lapatinib, pertuzumab in later trials; **none in GeparDuo, GeparTrio, PREPARE**). Endocrine therapy ≥5 years for ER/PgR-positive pts.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Protocols recommended adjuvant RT per national guidelines, with RNI indicated mainly by nodal stage. **No patient-level RT data were available**, so receipt, fields and dose are unknown.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **LRR as first event** (breast/chest wall, axillary, infra/supraclavicular nodes) measured from surgery; distant recurrence, second malignancy and death were competing events.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: 5-yr LRR **7.8% BCS vs 11.3% mastectomy**, but surgery type was **not an independent predictor** in multivariate analysis. Age, cN, grade, subtype and pCR were independent; **non-pCR HR 3.33** and **TNBC HR 2.72**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The authors place this alongside the EBCTCG meta-analysis, which found higher local recurrence after NACT than after adjuvant chemotherapy, especially with suboptimal local therapy. The NSABP B-51 question (RNI after nodal pCR) is the RT decision these data frame but cannot answer.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents pts with primary breast cancer, including cT4 and inflammatory disease, treated with anthracycline/taxane NACT in German cooperative-group trials. Does not represent pts given modern post-neoadjuvant escalation (T-DM1, capecitabine) or pts with known RT delivery.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Anti-HER2 therapy was **inconsistent across eras**, which the authors use to explain the lower LRR in HR+/HER2+ disease. gBRCA status incomplete; the univariate surgery effect is likely confounded by selection.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Biology and response drive LRR after NACT more than surgery type. The **non-pCR TNBC and HR-/HER2+** groups are where locoregional escalation has the most room to show benefit. With RT unrecorded, the low post-pCR rates are not evidence that RT can be omitted.

studies.interpretation:
The core message of this pooled analysis is that after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, locoregional risk follows tumour biology and response more than the operation. A crude gap between mastectomy and breast conservation (11.3% vs 7.8% at five years) vanishes once age, nodal stage, grade, subtype and pCR enter the model. That fits the authors' reading that mastectomy was given to higher-risk patients, and it should stop anyone from treating mastectomy after NACT as a local-control choice in itself. The decision that matters is what follows surgery.

For a radiation oncologist, the most useful output is the subtype-by-response grid. Without pCR, TNBC reached 18.5% and HR-/HER2+ 14.8% LRR at five years. With pCR, every subtype fell between 3.1% and 4.8%. In other words, achieving pCR erases most of the subtype gradient, and the high-risk tail sits almost entirely in residual-disease, hormone-receptor-negative tumours. Among pCR patients, only clinical node positivity hinted at residual risk (HR 1.61, p=0.054). That borderline signal is the part of the dataset most relevant to the current de-escalation debate. NSABP B-51 asked whether regional nodal irradiation can be dropped after nodal conversion, and this analysis neither supports nor undermines that question. It only shows that the baseline-node-positive, pCR population is not obviously risk-free.

The major caveat sets the ceiling on everything above: no patient-level radiotherapy data exist. Protocols recommended RT per guidelines, so most of these rates are presumably rates after some RT, but which patients got PMRT, which got nodal fields, and to what extent, is unknown. The low post-pCR LRR therefore cannot be read as the natural history of an untreated chest wall or nodal basin. It describes the outcome of a guideline-era mix of local therapy. The same problem cuts the other way for the high-risk groups. A TNBC non-pCR rate of 18.5% after presumably frequent RT points to radioresistance or systemic failure appearing locally first, not to an unirradiated population that RT would obviously rescue.

The treatment era limits generalisability. Several trials gave HER2-positive patients no anti-HER2 therapy, and none used post-neoadjuvant escalation with T-DM1 or capecitabine. Both have since improved outcomes in residual disease, though, as the authors note, their effect on LRR has not been reported. Contemporary non-pCR TNBC and HER2-positive patients probably carry lower locoregional risk than reported here, by an unknown margin. The HR+/HER2+ estimates are the most era-contaminated.

What would make this analysis misleading? A systematic link between RT omission and the high-risk strata, or the reverse, would distort any implied RT effect, and the dataset cannot test for either. It is best used as a risk-stratification map for designing and enrolling trials in post-neoadjuvant locoregional therapy, not as evidence for any individual RT decision.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Residual-disease TNBC (18.5%) and HR-/HER2+ (14.8%) carry the 5-yr LRR burden, while pCR flattens every subtype to 3.1-4.8%. RT delivery was unrecorded, so this sets risk strata for PMRT/RNI decisions after NACT rather than proving that RT can be omitted after pCR.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Mastectomy's crude LRR excess (11.3% vs 7.8% for BCS) disappears on multivariate analysis, and surgery type predicted LRR in no subtype. After NACT, choosing mastectomy over BCS did not independently improve local control; response and biology did.

open_questions: Is RNI or PMRT safely omitted after nodal pCR in initially cN+ pts?
Does locoregional RT escalation reduce LRR in non-pCR TNBC?
Do post-neoadjuvant T-DM1 or capecitabine lower LRR?

studies.name: PMRT selection in T1-T2, 1-3 node-positive breast cancer
studies.tldr: 10y KM LRR±SDR 15.9% without PMRT in pT1-T2 1-3 N+; age <45 with >25% nodes positive reached 58.0%.

details.text: 🔍 Retrospective population-based BCCA cohort, N=821, diagnosed 1989-1997, mastectomy without adjuvant RT
🔍 All had modified radical mastectomy + ALND; median 10 nodes removed (range 1-39)

details: ⚠️ 296 pts who received PMRT were excluded, so the no-RT cohort may be selected toward lower risk
💊 Systemic therapy in 94%: AC 202, CMF 91, FAC 4 of 302 chemo pts; tamoxifen in 581

details.text: 📊 10y KM ILRR 12.7% (SE 1.3), LRR±SDR 15.9% (SE 1.5); median f/u 7.7y
📊 10y KM BCSS 71.3%, OS 58.2%; distant recurrence 31.2% (n=256)
📊 Regional recurrence sites (n=57)
📐 Multivariable Cox: independent predictors of LRR
📊 Risk classification model, 10y KM LRR (Fig 1)
⚠️ >25% N+ ILRR CI 0.99-4.05 crosses 1 despite p=0.05
⚠️ Model breakpoints chosen by significance + subgroup size; no external validation; top-risk cell N=19
🔗 DBCG 82b/82c no-PMRT LRR ~30% at 10y vs this cohort's 13-16%, attributed to axillary staging + selection differences

verdict.rationale: Retrospective single-province no-RT cohort; excluded PMRT recipients; data-driven breakpoints, no validation set; pre-taxane, ALND-era systemic therapy limits transfer to modern pts.
verdict.audience: pT1-T2, 1-3 N+ breast after mastectomy + ALND, no PMRT

studies.significance: Clavicular nodes carried 19 of 57 regional recurrences (33%) versus 2 for internal mammary, so the residual risk this model flags sits mostly in the axillary-supraclavicular field. In women ≥45 with ≤25% nodes positive, 10y LRR±SDR was 10.8%, near the authors' <10% omission threshold, while medial or ER-negative tumors pushed that subset to approximately 20%.
studies.monday_clinic: In a woman ≥45 with a lateral, ER-positive pT1-T2 tumor and ≤25% of ALND nodes positive, this supports discussing PMRT omission; it does not extend to SLNB-only staging, where the nodal-ratio factor cannot be computed.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Retrospective population-based cohort from the BCCA Breast Cancer Outcomes Unit database. **N=821** of 1117 identified, after excluding **296 who received RT**. Cox multivariable modeling, then a classification model built from the significant factors. Median follow-up **7.7y**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **pT1-T2, 1-3 positive axillary nodes**, diagnosed 1989-1997, all treated with modified radical mastectomy and axillary dissection. Excluded pT3-T4, ≥4 N+, M1 and unknown pTN. Median age 62.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Adjuvant systemic therapy in **94%** per BCCA guidelines: chemo alone 21.7%, hormonal alone 57.1%, both 15.1%. Chemo was AC, CMF or FAC; hormonal therapy was mostly tamoxifen.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **No pt received locoregional RT**; the study defines baseline no-PMRT risk to inform selection, not RT efficacy. Authors anchor benefit estimates on an RT relative LRR reduction of **approximately two-thirds**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** isolated LRR (chest wall, axillary, infraclavicular, IMN as first site) and LRR±simultaneous distant recurrence. **Secondary:** BCSS and OS.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Overall 10y LRR±SDR **15.9%**. Each of age <45, T2, grade 3, ER-negative, medial location, >1 N+ or >25% N+ alone conferred **>20%** 10y LRR on univariate analysis. Age was the first model split (**29.3% vs 13.7%**, p<0.0001).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: No-PMRT LRR here (13-16% at 10y) sits well below the **~30%** in DBCG 82b/82c and nearer the BCCA randomized trial (**16% at 10y**) and systemic-therapy trial cohorts (**12-20%**). Authors attribute the gap to axillary staging, systemic therapy and selection differences.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents pT1-T2, 1-3 N+ women after mastectomy with full axillary dissection, treated with 1990s AC/CMF/tamoxifen-era systemic therapy and no PMRT. Does not represent SLNB-only axillary staging or pts on modern systemic regimens.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Excluding the 296 PMRT recipients likely removed higher-risk pts, biasing baseline risk downward. The **>25% nodes positive** ratio depends on ALND node yield, and its ILRR HR CI (0.99-4.05) touches 1. The ER status row in Table 1 shows a transposition in the source.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Authors propose **<10%** 10y LRR as a low-risk group that may be spared PMRT, **>30%** as justifying it, and **15-20%** as the threshold for discussion. The model supports considering PMRT in all women <45 and recommending it when >25% of nodes are positive.

studies.interpretation:
The value of this cohort is that it measures what happens to pT1-T2, 1-3 node-positive women when nobody irradiates them, in a population treated with adjuvant systemic therapy almost universally. That baseline is what the absolute benefit of PMRT depends on. The randomized evidence for PMRT in this group came largely from DBCG 82b and 82c, where no-PMRT locoregional recurrence ran near 30% at 10 years. Here it is 12.7% isolated and 15.9% with simultaneous distant recurrence, closer to the BCCA randomized trial and to the systemic-therapy trial cohorts the authors cite. If the relative reduction from RT is roughly constant, as the authors assume, a lower baseline shrinks the absolute gain, and the argument for routine PMRT in every 1-3 N+ woman weakens. This paper turns that observation into a selection tool.

The tool itself deserves less confidence than the baseline does. The breakpoints were chosen by looking at which splits gave the strongest statistical separation with workable subgroup sizes, inside the same dataset, with no validation cohort. Data-driven cutpoints tend to overstate separation, and the most striking cell, 58.0% LRR±SDR in women under 45 with more than 25% of nodes positive, rests on 19 women. The more transferable result is the multivariable model: age under 45, nodal ratio above 25%, medial location and ER-negative status hold up as independent predictors on both endpoints, with hazard ratios in the 2 to 3.7 range. Even there, the nodal-ratio estimate for isolated LRR has a lower bound of 0.99.

Two selection features pull in opposite directions. Excluding the 296 women who did receive RT probably removed pts their treating physicians judged higher risk, which would push the reported baseline down and make the low-risk group look safer than an unselected population. Against that, the cohort was staged with full axillary dissection and a median of 10 nodes removed, which is more thorough than much of the trial data the authors compare against and should reduce understaging. The nodal-ratio factor depends on dissection yield, so it does not carry over to a sentinel-node-only axilla, where the denominator is small by design.

The era matters more than the paper could anticipate. Systemic therapy was AC, CMF or FAC plus tamoxifen. Better systemic control lowers locoregional recurrence on its own, so the risk-group estimates here likely overstate what a comparable pt faces now, and the model's thresholds would need recalibrating rather than applying as printed. SUPREMO was designed to answer the 1-3 node-positive PMRT question prospectively, and its result is the natural test of whether risk-adapted selection of this kind holds.

For the RT reader, the pattern-of-failure data carry practical weight: a third of regional recurrences were clavicular and very few involved the internal mammary chain, which bears on target volumes when PMRT is chosen. The paper also gives a usable framework for counselling. Below about 10% the morbidity of PMRT is hard to justify; above about 30% it is hard to withhold; the middle band is a discussion. That framing has aged better than any specific cutpoint, and it is where this study still informs a decision.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Clavicular nodes carried 19 of 57 regional recurrences (33%) versus 2 for internal mammary, pointing PMRT coverage at the supraclavicular field. Age <45, >25% nodes positive, medial location and ER-negative status each moved 10y LRR above 20%, giving a factor-based frame for the 1-3 N+ PMRT discussion.

open_questions: Does the risk model validate with modern systemic therapy?
Nodal-ratio factor usable after SLNB-only axillary staging?
Do genomic risk scores refine PMRT selection in 1-3 N+?

studies.name: CPS+EG staging and local-regional recurrence after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
studies.tldr: 5-yr freedom from LRR by CPS+EG score spanned 71% to 99%, vs 86% to 97% by clinical or pathologic stage, in 1697 pts after NACT.
details: 🔍 Retrospective MD Anderson cohort, N=1697, treated 1997 to 2005, prospectively maintained database
🔍 CPS+EG = clinical stage + post-NACT pathologic stage + ER status + nuclear grade (AJCC 7th)
⚠️ Excluded pts given neoadjuvant trastuzumab and pts given preoperative RT

details.text: 🔍 Median f/u 51 mo (range 4 to 113)
📊 Crude LRR by local therapy (overall 6.5%, N=110)
📊 5-yr LRR-free survival by CPS+EG score
📊 PMRT-indicated cohort (cStage III or ypN+, N=1103): 5-yr LRR-free survival by local therapy

details: 📊 MVA: CPS+EG ≥3, ≥4 and ≥6 tied to higher LRR risk; ≥5 nonsignificant trend
📊 MVA: mastectomy alone significantly higher LRR risk vs BCT; PMRT marginally lower
⚠️ Table 5 row-level HRs not reliably attributable in source extraction; omitted here

details.text: ⚠️ Omission signal rests on 72 mastectomy-alone pts in the CPS+EG ≤2 subset

details: ⚠️ Confounding by indication: local therapy chosen by pt, surgeon and radonc, not randomized
⚠️ Text says mastectomy alone had HIGHER LRR-free survival in CPS+EG ≥3, contradicting the MVA; per-arm rates not in source text

details.text: ⚠️ Overall LRR given as 6.5% in Results and 6.1% in Discussion

details: ⚠️ RT dose, fractionation and target volumes not reported in source

details.text: 🔗 vs NSABP B-18/B-27 (cited): 10-yr LRR 10.3% BCT, 12.3% mastectomy, but no PMRT given

verdict.rationale: Retrospective single-institution cohort; the PMRT-omission claim rests on a non-randomized subgroup with confounding by indication and only 72 mastectomy-alone pts.
verdict.audience: Breast cancer post-NACT without trastuzumab, cStage III or ypN+

studies.significance: The PMRT read is in the CPS+EG ≤2 slice of the PMRT-indicated cohort (cStage III or ypN+): 5-yr LRR-free survival did not differ by local therapy (P=0.73), but only 72 pts had mastectomy alone. ER-positive or low-grade biology drives those low scores, so the proposed de-escalation gate is biology on top of residual nodal stage.
studies.monday_clinic: In cStage III or ypN+ disease after anthracycline/taxane NACT with ER-positive or low-grade biology (CPS+EG ≤2), this is hypothesis-level support for discussing PMRT omission; it does not extend to pts treated with neoadjuvant trastuzumab or to CPS+EG ≥3.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Retrospective** analysis of two MD Anderson cohorts used to build (932 pts, 1997 to 2003) and validate (804 pts, 2004 to 2005) CPS+EG; 39 excluded, **N=1697**. Median f/u **51 mo**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: All pts received **neoadjuvant anthracycline and/or taxane chemotherapy**; median age 50. **Neoadjuvant trastuzumab and preoperative RT excluded**; 20 pts missing ER or grade also excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Local therapy: BCT 656 (39%), mastectomy alone 297 (17%), mastectomy + PMRT 744 (44%). Institutional PMRT indications were **clinical stage III, ypN+, or select cT1/T2N1 with high-risk features**. Dose, fractionation and fields **not reported in source**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **LRR** = invasive cancer in ipsilateral breast, chest wall or regional nodes, counted regardless of distant timing. Objectives: CPS+EG vs stage for LRR stratification, and whether a score threshold could identify pts safely omitting PMRT.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: 5-yr freedom from LRR **71% to 99%** by CPS+EG vs **86% to 97%** by clinical or pathologic stage. In the PMRT-indicated cohort with **CPS+EG ≤2**, local therapy type made **no difference** (P=0.73).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: NSABP B-18/B-27 (cited) reported 10-yr LRR of 10.3% with BCT and 12.3% with mastectomy but gave no PMRT, so cannot address it. The MD Anderson Prognostic Index omitted ER and grade. NSABP B-51 later randomized regional nodal RT in cN+ → ypN0, a different population from the ypN+ pts here.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents non-trastuzumab NACT pts with cStage III or ypN+ disease and ER-positive or low-grade biology. Does not represent HER2+ pts treated with neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy or modern immunotherapy-containing regimens.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Prose direction for the CPS+EG ≥3 subgroup (mastectomy alone favored) contradicts the MVA; overall LRR is reported as both **6.5%** and **6.1%**. Median f/u of **51 mo** is short for ER-positive disease, the biology driving the favorable scores.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The stratification claim is sound and adds biology to anatomic staging for LRR. The omission claim is a null comparison in a small, selected subgroup with no equivalence margin, so it frames a trial question rather than settling one.

studies.interpretation:
This paper takes on a question randomized data had not answered when it was written: whether a pt with clinical stage III or residual node-positive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and mastectomy needs PMRT. The authors argue that anatomy alone overstates risk for a subset whose tumors are ER-positive or lower grade, and that adding those two biologic variables to clinical and pathologic stage widens the spread of 5-yr freedom from LRR to 71% to 99%, against 86% to 97% for either staging axis alone. That stratification claim is the paper's strongest contribution. It uses the whole 1697-pt cohort, it holds up on multivariate analysis, and it carries a scoring system the same group had already built and validated for disease-specific survival over to a local-regional endpoint.

The PMRT-omission claim is weaker, and the reason is structural rather than statistical. Local therapy was chosen by the pt, surgeon and radiation oncologist under an institutional policy that routed clinical stage III and ypN+ pts to PMRT. In the CPS+EG ≤2 slice of the PMRT-indicated cohort, the pts who did not get PMRT were pts someone had already judged to be lower risk, and there were only 72 of them. A null log-rank result (P=0.73) in a 358-pt group with few events shows no detectable difference; it does not show equivalence. No confidence interval on the between-arm difference and no non-inferiority margin are given, and confounding by indication runs in the direction that flatters omission.

The reporting also needs a careful read. For the CPS+EG ≥3 subgroup, the text states that LRR-free survival was higher with mastectomy alone, which conflicts with the multivariate model where mastectomy alone carried significantly higher LRR risk and PMRT was marginally protective. The figure and text agree on significance (0.0006 and <0.001) but the prose direction looks inverted. The crude overall LRR is given as 6.5% in Results and 6.1% in Discussion. Neither changes the central argument, but both are reasons to want the per-arm rates before quoting this subgroup in a tumor board.

Against the literature the authors cite, the pooled NSABP B-18/B-27 experience had higher LRR (10.3% with BCT, 12.3% with mastectomy) but did not deliver PMRT, so it cannot inform the omission question, and the MD Anderson Prognostic Index scored anatomic and pathologic features without ER or grade. NSABP B-51 later tested regional nodal RT prospectively, but in cN+ pts converted to ypN0; the residual ypN+ pts at the center of this paper sit outside that trial, so for them this retrospective signal remains close to the best available framing.

Transferability is the main constraint for a current reader. The cohort was treated from 1997 to 2005 with anthracycline and taxane regimens, and pts given neoadjuvant trastuzumab were excluded, so HER2-directed and immunotherapy-containing regimens, which change both pCR rates and the biology of residual disease, are not represented. RT technique is not described. The 51-month median follow-up matters most here: the low-score group is defined largely by ER-positivity, the biology in which local-regional events accrue late. The way this result would turn out wrong is late recurrence beyond 5 years in exactly the pts it proposes to spare.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The omission signal sits in ypN+ or cStage III pts with CPS+EG ≤2 (N=358, P=0.73 across local therapies), the group PMRT policy treats by default. Field design, dose and target volumes are not reported, so nothing here speaks to nodal coverage or de-escalated volumes, only to the yes/no PMRT decision.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Mastectomy alone carried the highest crude LRR (8.1% vs 5.5% BCT) and significantly higher LRR risk on MVA vs BCT. After NACT, choosing mastectomy does not reduce local-regional risk on its own; BCT outcomes held across the cohort.

open_questions: Is PMRT omission safe in ypN+ pts with CPS+EG ≤2 beyond 5 years?
Does CPS+EG stratify LRR after modern anti-HER2 or immunotherapy NACT?
Prospective validation of biology-based PMRT selection after NACT

studies.name: Long-term impact of regional nodal irradiation after neoadjuvant systemic therapy
studies.tldr: Adjusted LRR HR 0.497 and DR HR 0.731 with RNI after NAT in cN+ stage II-III breast; unadjusted 10-yr LRR 9.4% vs 8.1%, P=.62.
details: 🔍 Single-institution retrospective (MD Anderson), N=1289, treated 1989-2007
🔍 Stage II-III, cytologically confirmed axillary mets, NAT then BCS or mastectomy with ALND
🔍 RNI given to 1080/1289 (83.8%), at treating radiation oncologist's discretion
📊 Median f/u 10.2 yrs after definitive surgery; 162/1289 (12.6%) had LRR
📊 Axillary pCR in 368/1289 (28.5%); 10-yr LRR 9.7% no pCR vs 4.8% pCR, P=.006

details.text: 📊 Univariate 10-yr cumulative incidence, no RNI vs RNI

details: 📐 Multicovariate Cox, RNI vs no RNI (HER2+ without trastuzumab excluded)
📊 RNI did not affect DSS or OS on univariate or multicovariate analysis
⚠️ Univariate null flips to benefit only after adjustment: confounding by indication (RNI pts younger, LVSI+, higher cT/cN)
⚠️ LRR MVA in axillary pCR pts not attempted: too few events (n=19)
⚠️ Tangent details unavailable; high-tangent coverage in 'no RNI' pts unknown
⚠️ 51/162 LRRs excluded from LRR analysis because DM preceded LRR (competing risk)
🔗 Authors frame result as consistent with EORTC 22922 and MA.20 RNI benefit after adjuvant chemo

verdict.rationale: Retrospective, discretionary RNI with marked baseline imbalance; benefit appears only after covariate adjustment, univariate null. HER2+ trastuzumab DR signal is a subgroup estimate.
verdict.audience: cN+ stage II-III breast, NAT then BCS/mastectomy with ALND

studies.significance: The unadjusted 10-yr LRR curves barely separate (9.4% vs 8.1%), yet RNI held up in residual-nodal disease on MVA (HR 0.476), which is where most RNI is already given. The axillary pCR arm stays uninformative: 5.5% vs 4.6% with too few events to model, so it does not answer the omission question.
studies.monday_clinic: In cN+ breast with residual axillary disease after NAT and ALND, this supports keeping RNI in the plan; it does not establish safe RNI omission after axillary pCR.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Single-institution **retrospective** cohort, N=1289, 1989-2007. Median follow-up **10.2 yrs** after definitive surgery. LRR and DR by cumulative incidence with competing risks; Cox multicovariate models.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Stage II-III breast cancer with **cytologically confirmed axillary metastases**, NAT, then BCS or mastectomy **with ALND**. Axillary pCR in 368 (28.5%).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: RNI defined as RT purposely directed to at least one regional nodal basin, at physician discretion, given to **1080 (83.8%)**. Median breast/chest wall **50 Gy/25 fx**, median boost **10 Gy/5 fx**; institutional standard covered undissected axilla, SCV and IMN, with variable field design. Of 209 without RNI, 142 had no RT at all.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **LRR** (breast or regional nodes) and **DR** (LRR or DM, first event), plus DSS and OS.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Univariate RNI effect null for LRR and DR. Adjusted, RNI reduced **LRR (HR 0.497)** and **DR (HR 0.731)**, with the largest DR effect in HER2+ pts on trastuzumab (**HR 0.237**). **No DSS or OS effect.**

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Authors read the benefit as carrying over the LRR and DM reductions seen in **EORTC 22922** and **MA.20** after adjuvant chemo into the NAT setting. They contrast prior HER2+ series (Danish 82b/c, SweBCG91-RT) suggesting relative radioresistance, and the ALTTO subset showing no RNI effect.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents cN+ stage II-III breast cancer after NAT and ALND, mostly mastectomy. Does not represent SLNB-only axillary staging or the cN1 to ypN0 omission question NSABP B-51/RTOG 1304 tests.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: RNI pts had more adverse baseline features, so adjustment does heavy lifting. 'No RNI' may include unrecorded high tangents. Half the HER2+ cohort predated trastuzumab and was excluded from MVA, shrinking the subgroup behind the HR 0.237 estimate.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Supports RNI after NAT when nodal disease persists. **Does not settle omission after axillary pCR**; the authors defer that to B-51.

studies.interpretation:
The central tension in this paper is that the crude data and the adjusted data tell different stories. On the cumulative incidence curves, RNI did nothing visible: 10-year LRR 9.4% without and 8.1% with, and DR actually ran higher in the RNI group. Only after adjustment does RNI emerge as protective, halving LRR risk and trimming DR. That pattern is exactly what confounding by indication predicts. Physicians gave RNI to younger women with LVSI, higher clinical T and N category, and less response in breast and axilla, so the RNI group started out at higher risk. Adjustment for measured covariates is the right move, but it can only correct for what was recorded, and in a discretionary series the unrecorded reasons a radiation oncologist chose to treat the nodes (extent of residual disease beyond ypN category, imaging findings, extranodal extension) are the ones most likely to matter. A reader should treat the adjusted HRs as a plausible direction with an uncertain magnitude, not as an estimate of what RNI would achieve if randomly assigned.

The comparison group is also less clean than its label suggests. Two thirds of the patients without RNI received no radiation at all, so 'no RNI' here partly means 'no RT', and some LRR benefit may reflect breast or chest wall treatment rather than nodal coverage. In the other direction, tangent geometry was unavailable, so some 'no RNI' patients may have had incidental low axillary dose through high tangents. Those two biases push in opposite directions, and the paper cannot separate them.

The subgroup with the clearest clinical relevance, residual nodal disease after NAT, is also where the result is least surprising. An adjusted LRR HR of 0.476 in patients without axillary pCR fits what most radiation oncologists already do, and it is consistent with the authors' reading of EORTC 22922 and MA.20 as transferable to the neoadjuvant setting. The genuinely open question, whether nodes can be left alone after cN1 converts to ypN0, is the one this cohort cannot answer: 5.5% versus 4.6% LRR in pCR patients rests on too few events to model, and the authors explicitly defer to NSABP B-51/RTOG 1304.

The HER2+ trastuzumab DR signal (HR 0.237) is the most striking number and the most fragile. It comes from 145 patients, runs against prior series suggesting HER2+ disease gains less from RT, and predates dual HER2 blockade and post-neoadjuvant escalation for residual disease. It is hypothesis-generating at best.

The absence of any DSS or OS effect at 10 years is coherent with the randomized adjuvant trials and should temper any reading of the DR result as a survival argument. Practically, the nomogram is the more durable contribution: it lets a reader estimate absolute 10-year LRR from margins, grade, subtype and nodal response, which is the number that actually drives a coverage decision.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The unadjusted 10-yr LRR curves barely separate (9.4% vs 8.1%), yet RNI held up in residual-nodal disease on MVA (HR 0.476), where nodal coverage is already standard. The axillary pCR group (5.5% vs 4.6%) had too few events to model, so it cannot support omission.

open_questions: Is RNI omission safe after cN1 to ypN0 conversion?
Does the HER2+ RNI benefit persist with modern HER2-directed NAT?
Does the nomogram validate in an SLNB-staged cohort?
